response_text:
Looking at this PR carefully, I need to examine the behavioral changes, test accuracy, and breaking changes.

**Key observations:**

1. **`grouptype.py`**: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` changed from a concrete class (with a no-op `evaluate` returning `[]`) to an abstract class (`pass`). Since it now inherits from `StatefulDetectorHandler` which has `abc.ABC` plus abstract methods, it cannot be instantiated.

2. **`detector.py`**: The `evaluate` return type changed from `list` to `dict` — a breaking change for any subclass. Also, the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook is now called when status changes to non-OK.

3. **`models/detector.py`**: A new `group_type` property is added that performs a registry lookup on every access.

4. **Tests**: I spotted a copy-paste bug in `test_state_results_multi_group` where the value for `group_2` should be `10` (matching the data packet) but is `6`.

5. **Test gap**: No test exists for what happens when `build_occurrence_and_event_data` raises an exception.

findings.title: Copy-paste error in test_state_results_multi_group mock value
findings.body: The data packet is built with `{"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}` but `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` is called for `group_2` with value `6` instead of `10`. This is a copy-paste from the previous line. The test passes only because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` currently ignores its `value` parameter, so if the mock is later changed to incorporate the value (e.g., into the fingerprint or evidence), the test would fail in a confusing way rather than catching the real discrepancy.

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler changed from concrete to uninstantiable abstract class
findings.body: Previously `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(DetectorHandler[...])` defined a concrete `evaluate` that returned `[]`, so the class was instantiable and could serve as a working no-op handler referenced by `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler`. The new body is just `pass`, and since `StatefulDetectorHandler` is `abc.ABC` with abstract methods `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, any code that accesses `detector.detector_handler` for a `MetricAlertFire` group type will now raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler...`. Although the inline comment says these issues are not created yet, this is a silent regression of a previously working registration.

findings.title: DetectorHandler.evaluate return type contract break
findings.body: The abstract method signature was changed from `-> list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `-> dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. Any existing concrete subclass of `DetectorHandler` (inside or outside this repo) that returns a list will now fail at runtime with an `AttributeError` on `.values()` in `process_detectors`, or at type-check time. This is a breaking API change for a public abstract base and warrants a deprecation/migration note rather than a silent switch.

findings.title: No coverage for build_occurrence_and_event_data raising
findings.body: `evaluate_group_key_value` calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` inside the status-change branch. If the hook raises, `enqueue_state_update` and `enqueue_dedupe_update` have already mutated handler state but `commit_state_updates` will not run (exception propagates out of `evaluate` before `process_detectors` reaches the commit call). There is no test asserting the behavior in that failure path (does the dedupe get reset? are partial state updates visible on retry?), so this whole failure mode is uncharacterized.

findings.title: Detector.group_type re-queries registry on every access
findings.body: The new `group_type` property calls `grouptype.registry.get_by_slug(self.type)` every time it is accessed, and `detector_handler` reads it on every invocation. In `process_detectors` and any caller that does `detector.detector_handler` repeatedly (e.g., per-detector loops, tests, API serializers), this triggers an unnecessary registry lookup each time. Caching the slug→GroupType lookup on the instance would avoid the repeated calls.
